scope_note: Dependency resolution and upstream qualification only. This file records resolved pins and observed evidence; it does not claim upstream behavior beyond what was executed. Regenerate via the named commands when changing any pin; do not edit go.mod pins independently of this report. Revision 2 (P02, implementation-remediation) reconciled this report against the actual source tree after revision 1 left a stale forward-looking claim in qualified_features: fyne.io/fyne/v2 was removed from go.mod/go.sum on 2026-09-19 (fdba444, following ADR 002's Flutter replacement of the native Go desktop six days earlier), but the prior revision still asserted 'Fyne v2.8.1 compiles and links' as though it were a current qualified feature. That claim is moved to historical_evidence below, clearly labeled as a fact about a build that no longer exists in the module graph, not a current qualification. No fyne import remains anywhere in Go source; the only surviving string 'fyne' is packaging/desktop_test.go asserting the framework is rejected as capability_unsupported.

historical_evidence.removal_reason: ADR 002 (2026-09-13 in spirit, decided 2026-09-15/18) replaced the native Go desktop with the Flutter client at apps/desktop, retiring internal/desktop and cmd/zatiti-desktop. Fyne was only still required because the root anchor file tools_deps.go held it behind a build tag; once cobra, the MCP Go SDK and modernc.org/sqlite had real package imports, go mod tidy dropped the anchor and Fyne with it, along with its transitive testify, go-spew, go-difflib and yaml.v3.
historical_evidence.historical_note: Prior to removal, Fyne v2.8.1 compiled and linked via cgo on darwin/amd64 under the then-pinned toolchain. This is a historical fact about a build configuration that no longer exists; it is NOT a current qualification claim, the module is not in go.mod/go.sum, and nothing in this repository imports it. Do not cite this entry as evidence that any current desktop framework claim is qualified.

external_services.resolution: Every MEMORY_VERBS capability stays explicitly blocked at this pin: PROTOCOL.md's own gap table shows row 1 (one Invoke = one physical request) fails against the documented three-request MCP session handshake, which blocks every other row independently of their individual gaps (no UUID claim ids, no command identity/status lookup, no revision report, no enforceable cost/destination bound, no verifiable running commit). internal/adapters/serenity/adapter_test.go exercises the adapter as an honest refuser against these fixtures; that is controlled-fixture evidence only. No live Serenity process has been contacted (PROTOCOL.md: 'read-only... no live Serenity process was contacted'). Required to lift any row to Provided: the upstream changes PROTOCOL.md's closing section names (sessionless call path, stored caller command identity with status lookup, UUID-compatible claim identities, revision reporting, per-call spend/destination bounds, a build that reports its commit) plus a real-service qualification run recorded under tests/qualification.
